components.css: .ds-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 24px; height: 56px; padding: 0 32px; background: var(--bar, #13293d); color: var(--bar-foreground, #e8f1f2); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--bar-border, #24425a); font-family: 'Archivo Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-brand { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; font-weight: 700; font-size: 18px; font-stretch: 118%; letter-spacing: -0.015em; } .ds-brand-tile { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 32px; height: 32px; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--bar-active, #1b98e0); color: var(--depth-4-foreground, #06131e); font-weight: 800; font-stretch: 118%; } .ds-tabs { display: flex; height: 100%; } .ds-tab { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 100%; padding: 0 12px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--bar-muted, #a9c1cf); text-decoration: none; transition: color 150ms; outline: none; } .ds-tab::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 12px; right: 12px; bottom: 0; height: 2px; background: var(--bar-active, #1b98e0); transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left; transition: transform 500ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--bar-foreground, #e8f1f2); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--bar-active, #1b98e0); } .ds-tab-active { color: var(--bar-foreground, #e8f1f2); } .ds-tab-active::after { transform: scaleX(1); }

narrative.overview:
Hostly reads a rental season like a nautical chart of the coast. The brand's blue family becomes the chart's depth tints, lines are 1px hairlines, and numbers are soundings: how many nights a property has booked this month is written on a cell whose water is as deep as the month is full. The calendar is chart water, its month days carrying faint contour lines (isobaths) that run on across the cells; days of other months are shoal and recede. Every stay is traced across its nights in its property's ink.

The chart's title block is a Prussian top bar that carries the brand, the section tabs and the account. Below it, everything sits on pale chart paper in light mode or a deep navy night chart in dark mode, divided by hairlines and grid lines rather than lifted into boxes. The type is one variable family, Archivo: titles set wide like chart lettering, UI at normal width, secondary labels in italic like the names of waters, figures tabular. Density is that of a working tool: 14px body text, 36px controls, 6px corners.

The world refuses two things: the gray SaaS dashboard of stacked cards, and nautical costume. There is no compass rose, no anchor, no illustrated map; the chart lives only in the depth tints, the contour lines, the graticule and the soundings.
keyCharacteristics: One blue family (Prussian, Sapphire, Celadon, Carolina, Azure), stepped into six depth tints that encode occupancy; sand is the one warm note.
Eight property inks, fixed per property across every screen.
A Prussian top bar as the brand field; no sidebar.
Archivo Variable only: wide titles (118%), italic water labels, tabular figures. Never a serif.
Hairlines, grid lines and tonal fields instead of shadows; contour lines and a graticule as the only texture.
Motion that surfaces, fills like a tide and traces a course; nothing moves under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth tints encode exactly one thing: how booked a property is. They fill sounding cells and nothing else that carries meaning; never use a depth step for status, emphasis or decoration.

rules.name: The Property Ink Rule
rules.body: Property inks identify a property (stay bars, the key dot on a sounding, list dots) and do nothing else, always with their paired foreground for text. Never use them for status or emphasis, and never let a property change ink between screens.

rules.name: The Bar Rule
rules.body: The top bar is the brand field: the `bar` family (Prussian in light, a deeper `bar-dark` at night), Azure text, muted tabs in `bar-muted`, and Carolina as the only action color on it. The auth panel and the public header are the same field. Nothing else in the app is Prussian-filled.

rules.name: The Theme Token Rule
rules.body: Colors come from theme classes (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`, `bg-depth-4`, `bg-bar`), never loose hex values in components, and every combination must work in light and dark.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo Variable is the only face. Hierarchy comes from width, weight and size; never introduce a second family, and never a serif.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Money, counts, dates and soundings use tabular figures (`tabular-nums`; tables get it globally).

rules.name: The Line-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Group with a grid line, a hairline or a tonal field first. A shadow appears only where something floats (overlays) or on the landing's two framed objects. Stay bars carry no shadow.

dos: Do take every color from a theme token and check it in light and dark.
Do use the depth tints only for occupancy, through `depthOf`, with each step's paired foreground.
Do keep each property's ink fixed across the calendar, the soundings key and the lists.
Do keep the brand on the Prussian bar, with Carolina as its only action color.
Do set titles wide (`font-wide`) and secondary explanatory labels italic (`font-water`), and use tabular figures for money, dates and soundings.
Do separate data with grid lines and hairlines; let the grid-line color show through the gaps.
Do start motion from a visible state with ease-out-expo, and let reduced motion turn it off.
donts: Don't use a serif, or any face other than Archivo Variable.
Don't add decorative map ornament: no compass roses, anchors, rope, waves, ships or illustrated maps. The chart is depth tints, contour lines, graticule and soundings.
Don't put the graticule anywhere but chart surfaces: the landing hero ground and the auth panel. Contour water belongs to the calendar's month days.
Don't change the bookings calendar's structure; change only its surface.
Don't use depth tints or property inks for status, emphasis or decoration.
Don't write loose hex or rgb values in components.
Don't add a sidebar; sections are tabs on the top bar.
Don't reach for a shadow where a line or a tonal field would separate the content.
